editorial.marketOverview: Tuesday cash trading has confirmed the expected semiconductor retracement. At 13 ET Nasdaq futures were down 1.79% against S&P futures down 0.47%, while Dow and Russell futures were positive. This indicates technology-specific weakness rather than uniform risk liquidation.
editorial.whatChanged: The prior premarket downside risk is now visible in cash stock losses. The 11 ET secondary futures report showed Nasdaq down 2.36%, versus 1.79% at 13 ET, suggesting partial stabilization rather than accelerating losses. Open Watch remains at 178 events with unchanged update timestamp.
editorial.marketInterpretation: Nvidia, Intel and Sandisk weakness supports the fragile reversal diagnosis. Easing yields reported by Reuters offer an offset, but oil has rebounded and December tightening expectations remain elevated. Direct breadth and synchronized volatility are missing, so a durable bearish regime is not yet established.
editorial.threeDayPath: Tuesday remainder remains vulnerable to chip selling, with some intraday stabilization. Wednesday PCE, GDP and earnings reactions can reset the rates and AI narrative. Friday shortened trading may amplify moves in either direction; Thursday closed.
editorial.bullCase: If semiconductor losses narrow further and QQQ recovers alongside lower yields and volatility, Monday's rebound could resume. Benign inflation and constructive hardware guidance would reinforce this path.
editorial.bearCase: A return to session lows, broader chip selling and hot inflation would raise the likelihood of a failed rebound. Rising oil and hawkish policy expectations could compound valuation pressure.
editorial.watchNext: Monitor cash QQQ and SOX relative returns, direct Nasdaq breadth, VXN/VIX and paired Treasury yields; Dell and HP guidance after close, then Wednesday PCE and GDP. Do not infer breadth from selected stock quotes.
